summary: M1-AC is the as-cast condition of the Si-free low-density medium-Mn steel M1 (nominal composition Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C), produced by vacuum arc melting and remelted four times with flipping between remelts. In the context of this study it is the starting material of the M1 alloy, taken before homogenization (1100 °C/2 h + water quenching), hot rolling (~50 % reduction at 1100–900 °C) and intercritical annealing (700 °C/1 h + water quenching), which define M1-HQ, M1-HR and M1-IA respectively. The paper's core questions — whether 3 % Al improves strength–ductility balance and how austenite is stabilized during intercritical annealing — are addressed on the downstream conditions, not on the as-cast state.
composition: Nominal composition Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C (M1), i.e. Fe base with about 8 wt% Mn, 3 wt% Al and 0.2 wt% C, as reported in the alloy-design calculations that use wt.% for compositional axes. The M1 alloy was deliberately defined as the maximum Al addition (3 %) to the Fe–8Mn-0.2C system that does not introduce δ-ferrite in the intercritical temperature range. Al is added as a lightweight element to lower steel density and to widen the intercritical temperature (ICT) window, which increased from 88 °C for the Al-free (0Al) composition to 300 °C for 3Al. This composition differs from the companion alloy M2 (Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C), in which 1 % Si is added at the cost of introducing δ-ferrite into the ICT range.
